agronomic_performance_field_trials: PL 807 has been utilized as a check variety in the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Wheat and Barley trials. Its yield performance and ancillary characters (e.g., Leaf Blight resistance) have been evaluated against check varieties like PL426 over multiple years in various locations, including Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs) at farmers' fields.

agronomic_performance_yield: Phule Vikram has demonstrated its ability to boost productivity and economic benefits, as evidenced by its adoption by farmers. In one study, the genotype Phule Vikram recorded a maximum yield per plant of 13.80 g, suggesting a high individual plant yield potential. However, a quantitative average yield in quintals per hectare (q/ha) is not specified.

agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Phule Vikram exhibits a tall growth habit, making it suitable for mechanical harvesting. It produces medium-sized, yellowish-brown seeds. It has also been described as semi-erect.

agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) On-farm trial, KVK Angul, 2024: Smarak was one of three technology options against Nali rasi. (2) Multi-varietal trial under organic management, Gangetic plains of West Bengal: treatment T-7, statistically comparable to T-5 (1375 kg/ha), gave the highest seed yield (1765 kg/ha) from the Smarak variety, with 52.64% oil content. (3) OUAT Central Farm, Rabi 2014-15: five varieties (Uma, Amrit, Smarak, Prachi, Nirmala) were tested with growth regulators NAA, GA3 and IAA. The digest does not report yield results for Smarak from this trial. agronomic_performance_field_trials: GNRB-1 has been part of numerous agricultural evaluations and recommendations. It served as a check variety in comparisons with other brinjal genotypes (e.g., GRB 5, Swarna Mani Black, GOB 1) and in line x tester mating designs. Trials include assessing its response to foliar application of Novel Organic Liquid Nutrients and its performance as seedlings under protected cultivation/polyhouse conditions. It has been recommended in AGRESCO meetings and annual reports of agricultural universities.
genetics_and_qtl_molecular_mechanisms: GNRB-1 is used as a standard check in line x tester mating designs for studying gene action. Hybrids involving GNRB-1, such as GNRB-1 × CH-215 and GNRB-1 × NBL-5, have been developed to increase fruit yield through heterosis and are also screened for tolerance to anaerobic germination, submergence, and drought. The presence of anthocyanin on the stem and young purple-green leaves is a distinguishing morphological characteristic.

agronomic_performance_yield: Mean yield 38 t/ha fresh rhizome, with up to 52 t/ha under favourable conditions; 30% and 34% higher than national and local varieties, per the institute page and the ResearchGate record. Pooled yield over three years was 14.52 kg per 3 m2 plot for Acc. 48, the highest of the accessions tested. The CSC average_yield field gives 30000 to 40000 Kg/Ha, which is broadly consistent with the 38 t/ha mean.
agronomic_performance_stability: The Kerala trial at AICRPS centres (2013-16), on-farm trials and yield stability were reported only as table captions in the source; no stability values were given in the digest. The three-year pooled yield is the only multi-season figure found.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: The CSC adaptation_ecology field recommends release and cultivation in Haryana, Punjab and Delhi under irrigated conditions. The digest does not corroborate this and reports trials in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The CSC recommended states (Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh) are also not corroborated by digest findings. The CSC adaptation and recommended-state fields are therefore in conflict and unverified against the digest.
agronomic_performance_maturity_days: 45 To 60Days (CSC record). Conflict: digest sources report a crop duration of 180 days, and some extension sources give 180-200 days. This discrepancy is unresolved.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu on-farm trial: rhizome rot 4.51% in IISR Pragati versus 2.12% in CO2; leaf blotch and leaf spot less frequent in IISR Pragati than CO2; all three varieties showed rhizome rot, leaf blotch and leaf spot. (2) Kerala trial 2013-16 at AICRPS centres with on-farm trials and yield stability reported; results are given only as table captions, so no values were available. (3) Three-year pooled trial: 14.52 kg per 3 m2 plot for Acc. 48, the highest of the tested accessions. (4) Greenhouse and field trial of 21 genotypes (2021-23): IISR Pragati gave high fresh yield per clump and high curcuminoids in some seasons. (5) Genetic variation study on turmeric genotypes: highest fresh rhizome yield per clump for IISR Pragati. (6) Quality traits: curcumin 5.02%, oleoresin 15.29%, essential oil 6.3%, dry recovery 15.95%. CSC agronomic_features also report excellent colour, very good keeping quality (13 days at room temperature), and good yield at 60 x 60 cm spacing with 80-90 kg N + 60 kg P2O5, plus weed control with 1-1.5 kg a.i. Stomp/HAT applied 3-4 days after transplanting; these are CSC-recorded features, not digest trial results.

(6) Assam (Jorhat) 2023-24 trial of Gujarat-bred genotypes: GCH 09 ranked among the most promising. The attribution to this variety is assumed from the name 'GCH 09' and is not confirmed. (7) ARS Mandor (Jodhpur) kharif 2022 trial: JHB 1018 among hybrids, recording the highest effective branches per plant (18.8).

agronomic_performance_yield: LCA-625 is a high-yielding chilli variety, with an reported yield advantage of 25-35% (RESULT_10, RESULT_18, RESULT_28). In an advanced yield trial of hot pepper, it recorded a dry pod yield of 6750 kg/ha (RESULT_7, RESULT_23). It has also recorded the highest dry fruit yield per plant in certain evaluations (RESULT_8, RESULT_17). In another assessment, it recorded a high yield of 12.6 (units not specified) (RESULT_48).
agronomic_performance_stability: LCA-625 is noted for its high color and high pungency (RESULT_4, RESULT_13, RESULT_35, RESULT_49). While general statements about hybrids adapting better to stress are made (RESULT_15), specific data on LCA-625's yield stability across diverse environments is not detailed.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Recommended for cultivation in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh (RESULT_28). It is considered ideal for dry chilli production (RESULT_33).
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: LCA-625 is a single cross derivative of G-4 x LCA-334 (Original data). Plants are described as tall with strong stems (RESULT_33). Fruits exhibit high color and high pungency (RESULT_4, RESULT_13, RESULT_35, RESULT_49). Starch content is reported at 24-26% (RESULT_6). It is an open-pollinated variety (RESULT_30, RESULT_46).
agronomic_performance_field_trials: LCA-625 has been evaluated in advanced yield trials for hot pepper (RESULT_7, RESULT_23, RESULT_24) and performance studies for yield and fruit quality (RESULT_14, RESULT_37). It was part of studies on photosynthesis-related parameters (RESULT_3, RESULT_11, RESULT_21, RESULT_34). Field studies involving LCA-625 have been conducted in Anakapalli District of Andhra Pradesh (RESULT_9, RESULT_19, RESULT_25, RESULT_40, RESULT_42). It has also been identified as a good general combiner for fruit number in breeding studies (RESULT_47).
genetics_and_qtl_molecular_mechanisms: In vitro screening of LCA-625 has been conducted to study proline concentration under stress, which is generally considered to confer tolerance to water deficit, suggesting research into physiological responses to stress (RESULT_1, RESULT_12, RESULT_31). The variety is a single cross derivative of G-4 x LCA-334 (Original data).

agronomic_performance_yield: Seed yield of 2001 kg/ha, which is 24-25% above the two checks. Comparative table: 2.6-2.8 t/ha in non-stress and 2.0-2.2 t/ha under salt stress. agronomic_performance_stability: Outperformed checks over four years for seed and oil yield under moderate to high salinity and alkalinity. Performed better in the All India Salinity Alkalinity Tolerant Variety Trials across salinity and alkalinity sites in Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Suited to salt-affected soils and timely sown conditions, with sowing recommended up to 25 October. Source record recommends a seed rate of 5 kg/ha and describes the variety as highly responsive to fertilizers. The newsletter also lists Delhi and Rajasthan (North Western Plain Zone) under salt stress and timely sown conditions.

agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Plant height about 180 cm; 6 primary branches; 9 secondary branches; main shoot 85 cm; 1000-seed weight 5.5 g; oil content 39-40%.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: Replicated yield trials ran for three years at five locations per year under saline and alkaline soils in Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, under AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard, against national checks including CS54, RH749 and Kranti. The variety performed better in the All India Salinity Alkalinity Tolerant Variety Trials at salinity and alkalinity sites across Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh. It outperformed the checks over four years for seed and oil yield under moderate to high salinity and alkalinity. Seed yield of 2001 kg/ha was 24-25% above two checks. Under ECe 9-11 dS/m, seed yield was 25% and oil yield 29% above checks CS54, Kranti and RH 0749. Reported 2.0-2.2 t/ha seed yield under saline and alkaline conditions.

agronomic_performance_yield: Average about 5,500 kg/ha (ResearchGate figure). CRRI table: 5.2 t/ha. CSC record: 5000-6000 kg/ha. Nagapattinam on-farm: 5,990 kg/ha after 16 days submergence. Khurda, Odisha (6-9 days submergence): 3.66 t/ha.
agronomic_performance_stability: Yield advantage of 1 t/ha or more under submergence, equal to Swarna when not submerged (Odisha head-to-head). Randomised trial in 128 Orissa villages showed about 45% gain over the popular variety after 10 days submergence, with no yield penalty without flooding. Poorer grain filling under stagnant flooding. Yield stability across non-submergence environments beyond these sites: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: CSC record: suitable for shallow lowland areas of coastal Odisha where Swarna is grown. Also grown in Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu (on-farm demonstrations) and Hooghly, West Bengal (management trial).
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: 1. STRAW COLOUR HULL 2. DARK GREEN LEAVES. Plant height about 100 cm; medium grain (digest). Shattering of grain during harvest and transport reported by farmers in Odisha. CSC record also notes medium slender grains with good cooking quality and suitability for late planting.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Odisha head-to-head project: survived 14 days complete submergence; Sub1 genotypes out-yielded non-Sub1 under flash flooding; yield advantage of 1 t/ha or more under submergence, equal to Swarna when not submerged. (2) CRRI table: tolerates 15-17 days submergence, 5.2 t/ha, duration 145 days (MS). (3) Bihar/IRRI data: 2-day submergence 98% survival vs about 94% for Swarna; after 4 days damage 5-9% vs 20-70% for other varieties. (4) Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu on-farm: 5,990 kg/ha after 16 days submergence, 22% over BPT 5204; 50 demonstration locations in 2011-12; low pest and disease incidence; lodging tolerant. (5) Randomised trial, 128 Orissa villages: about 45% yield gain over popular variety after 10 days submergence, no penalty without flooding. (6) Management trial at Chinsurah, Hooghly, West Bengal (kharif 2011) on nursery and main-field options; results not stated in digest. (7) Khurda, Odisha, 6-9 days submergence: average 3.66 t/ha for Swarna-Sub1 vs 2.25 t/ha for non-Sub1. (8) Nature study: grain filling poorer than Swarna under stagnant flooding.
genetics_and_qtl_qtl_information: Sub1 locus on chromosome 9 is the main contributor to flood tolerance (no effect sizes or marker positions given in the digest).

Farmers in Odisha partly adopted the variety for resistance to sheath blight (farmer feedback, not a confirmed resistance rating). Bacterial blight resistance: no evidence found for this variety (the xa5/xa13/Xa21 line is CR Dhan 800, excluded). Pest and disease incidence was reported as low in Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu demonstrations.
pest_resistance_summary: CSC record: pest reaction unknown. The CRRI table lists tolerance to stem borer, leaf folder, whorl maggot and rice hispa in a row adjacent to the Swarna Sub1 entry, but the text extraction is ambiguous, so these ratings are unconfirmed for this variety and are not attributed. drought_details_research: No evidence found for this variety in the digest. Drought-resilience reports relate to CR Dhan 801/802, which were excluded as separate varieties.
flood_details_research: Released as a flood-tolerant version of Swarna. Tolerant to flash flood submergence (CSC record). Under flash flooding in Odisha, Sub1 genotypes gave higher yield than non-Sub1 genotypes. Limitation: grain filling was poorer than Swarna under stagnant flooding (medium-depth stagnation). Water-stagnation tolerance per se has no separate evidence for this variety.
submergence_details_research: Complete submergence tolerance for about 14-17 days, versus 4-5 days for Swarna. Tolerates up to 15-17 days of complete submergence (CRRI table). Survived 14 days of complete submergence. Sub1 locus on chromosome 9 is the main contributor to flood tolerance. Under 2-day submergence, 98% survival versus about 94% for Swarna. After 4 days, damage was 5-9% versus 20-70% for other varieties (Bihar/IRRI data). Yield advantage of 1 t/ha or more under submergence, with yield equal to Swarna when not submerged.

Quality (IARI Indore newsletter source): grain hardness index 81.4, chapatti score 7.86, biscuit score 6.73, test weight 81.8 kg/hl, sedimentation value 44.8 ml. Micronutrients and protein (commercial IndiaMart listing, secondary): iron about 38 ppm, zinc about 37 ppm, protein above 12%.

disease_resistance_summary: Stem rust and leaf rust: seedling resistance (all-stage) to all 27 test pathotypes each of stem and leaf rust (ResearchGate IARI Indore newsletter source). High field resistance to stem rust (ACI max 1.5, mean 0.9) and leaf rust (ACI max 3.1, mean 1.6). High adult-plant resistance to stem rust pathotypes 40A and 117-6 and leaf rust pathotypes 77-5, 77-9 and 104-2. The stem rust gene Sr31 is postulated for resistance to all Indian pathotypes, but it is not confirmed as a gene in this variety (CSC release paper). Good resistance reported to leaf blight, Karnal bunt, Fusarium head blight, loose smut, foot rot and flag smut (ResearchGate source). Black/brown rust and Karnal bunt resistance reported by a trade news site (global-agriculture.com). The IARI Regional Station page lists resistance to stem and leaf rust, flag smut, leaf blight, root rot and Karnal bunt. A translated IARI page lists resistance to all three rusts, Karnal bunt, powdery mildew, flag smut and foot rot; this is a mixed-content page and should be treated with caution. disease_resistance_summary: Foliar disease resistance (CSC record): resistant to foliar diseases under natural and artificial epiphytotic conditions. Resistance to rusts, particularly brown rust, is useful under timely-sown conditions in NEPZ. Race-specific APR responses to brown rust races 77-5, 77-9 and 104-2 were recorded across locations. Seedling resistance tests (SRT) indicated resistance to the prevalent brown rust race 77-7, and to races 77-8, 77-9, 77-10, 104-2, 104-3, 104B, 162-2 and 162A. Yellow and brown rust: listed as resistant in two commercial sources. Stripe and leaf rust: resistant, with high resistance to wheat blast, moderate resistance to Karnal bunt and loose smut tolerance in one commercial source. Wheat blast: high resistance reported in a seed-production case study. Multiple disease resistance: described in a bread-wheat evaluation paper. CONFLICT: the commercial source listing stripe and leaf rust resistance does not match the yellow and brown rust listing from the other sources; the rust type should be checked against the CSC record. The CSC record indicates resistance to brown, black and yellow rusts.
drought_details_research: The digest reports that DBW 187 was ranked as tolerant to both heat and drought stress in a backcross-inbred-line (BIL) QTL mapping study. No quantitative drought measurement is given. The digest also states that no drought-specific evidence was found in the searches. Level is assigned as medium because the only evidence is a qualitative tolerant ranking. Under late sowing, the variety showed less yield reduction than the check DBW 39, which is consistent with a stress-adapted profile but is not a drought measurement.
heat_details_research: CSC record: heat sensitivity index (HSI) of 1.05, described as better tolerance to heat stress. Under late-sown conditions the variety performed better than all checks, with minimum reduction in grain yield, grain number and 1000-grain weight, indicating better adaptation to heat stress. In the 2021-22 AICRP demonstrations under heat, DBW 187 gave a 3.6% yield gain over HD-3086. It was ranked as tolerant to both heat and drought in a BIL study. The digest does not state the genetic basis of heat tolerance.

disease_resistance_summary: No pathogen resistance is attributed to GJG-5 in the searched sources. The little leaf disease finding in the combined FVegetableCropsVR.pdf proforma was excluded because its attribution is uncertain beside brinjal material. The little leaf and jassid tolerance statement in Variety-11-years.pdf was excluded because it belongs to a different crop. Stem rot, thrips and jassid tolerance is not established for GJG-5; the JAU report's stem rot, jassid and thrips tolerance belongs to a groundnut variety and was excluded. Separately, the JAU proforma (Variety-13-years.pdf) reports that the rabi clonal-selection garlic (named Gujarat Junagadh Garlic 5 (GJG 5) on the source) was tolerant of bolting and jointed bulbs, with lower bolting and jointed-bulb percentages than the check varieties. Bolting and jointed bulbs are physiological disorders rather than pathogens, so they are reported here for completeness and not as disease resistance.

agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Organic versus conventional trial (farming systems and garlic clones): Yamuna Safed-9 gave the highest bulb yield under inorganic management, at 78.33 q/ha. (2) Eastern Dry Zone of Karnataka: Yamuna Safed-9 was among the genotypes with the best growth and yield, reported at 12.10 t/ha in the South India comparison. (3) Mandor (Agriculture Research Station, Agriculture University Jodhpur, rabi 2015-16), 13 genotypes: Yamuna Safed-9 showed maximum plant height, bulb diameter and bulb yield of 9.46 t/ha. (4) Thrips and purple blotch reaction study in South India: the variety is among the genotypes tested, but no resistance class is given (see stress_tolerance). A planting-date trial at Nashik and Karnal on Yamuna Safed-group garlic is excluded because it does not name Yamuna Safed-9.

agronomic_performance_yield: Reported yields for DGGV-2 vary across studies. It was observed as a 'lowest yielder' at 393 kg/ha in one analysis. Another study recorded a seed yield of 701.3 kg/ha. However, with optimal management (sowing during the first fortnight of June and foliar spray of 2% DAP), DGGV-2 demonstrated a higher seed yield of 1380 kg/ha.
agronomic_performance_stability: The varying yield performance across different studies (393 kg/ha, 701.3 kg/ha, 1380 kg/ha) suggests its yield can be influenced by environmental conditions and specific agronomic practices.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: DGGV-2 is suitable for sowing up to the end of June but not suitable for late sowing. It exhibits tolerance to shattering compared to Chinamung and Sel-4 varieties. It is responsive to fertilizer application at 25 N & 50 P kg/ha. Optimal performance was noted with first fortnight of June sowing combined with 2% DAP foliar spray.

agronomic_performance_yield: Average yield of 994 kgs/ha was originally reported. Specific trials showed variations, with yields up to 1409 kg/ha (14.09 q/ha) in comparison trials, and 912 kg/ha (9.12 q/ha) in specific regional projects (Jammu, 2015-2016). It serves as a standard check variety against which newer varieties exhibit yield superiority.
agronomic_performance_stability: Demonstrates low genotype x environment interaction, indicating good yield stability across different environments.

agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Seed are shiny green and medium seed size with high protein content.

genetics_and_qtl_molecular_mechanisms: Physiological responses associated with stress tolerance in IPM 02-3 include overaccumulation of glycine betaine, higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD), Membrane Stability Index (MSI), and total chlorophyll content under stress conditions.

disease_resistance_summary: Rust: the ORS Tindivanam page reports the culture as completely resistant to rust disease; the EJPB paper reports only moderate resistance to rust compared with check varieties. These sources conflict and the conflict is unresolved. Late leaf spot (LLS): the ORS page reports tolerance with a score of 2.0; the EJPB paper reports moderate resistance compared with check varieties; a separate leaf spot score reports a medium resistant reaction (score 6.0) against 9.0 for susceptible checks VRI 2, CO 2 and TMV 2. Multiple sources agree on LLS tolerance or moderate-to-medium resistance, though the scales differ.
pest_resistance_summary: TMV 14 showed tolerance to Spodoptera litura, thrips, Helicoverpa armigera and leaf miner (reported in the EJPB paper and the Academia.edu copy of the same work). No quantitative pest scores were found.
drought_details_research: No TMV 14-specific drought result was found. A PEG-6000 germination screen (Umadevi et al.) lists TMV 14 in a table, but the retrieved text does not show its classification, so it is not counted as a finding. The rainfed trials cited elsewhere report yields, not drought-tolerance classifications.

agronomic_performance_adaptation: CSC record: Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand under rainfed/irrigated kharif and summer seasons. Suitable for early sowing conditions. Sowing-date trial in Telangana (Northern zone) found best performance with sowing up to late August. Vikaspedia and the ICAR-IIMR brochure also list Telangana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh; these are not part of the CSC recommended state list.

agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Kharif 2014, S.V. Agricultural College Farm, Tirupati (sandy loam, Southern Zone of Andhra Pradesh): SiA 3085 gave the highest growth, yield attributes and yield among four varieties; 50 kg N/ha was profitable. (2) Sowing-date trial, Telangana (Northern zone): best performance with sowing up to late August. (3) Rainfed Andhra Pradesh: highest grain yield of 1141 kg/ha among tested entries (secondary review citation). (4) AMMI analysis of rainfed Andhra Pradesh genotypes: narrow adaptation to Anantapur. (5) Frontline demonstrations (FLDs) in Northeast India (Arunachal Pradesh, CAU Pasighat) and Tripura (SARS): SiA-3085 demonstrated; no yield values in the digest. (6) Included as a released check in a foxtail core collection of 223 accessions (genetic diversity context, not a yield trial).

disease_resistance_summary: No specific disease is named as resisted by DHLM-28-4 in any source. A ResearchGate-hosted promotional page describes the variety as having pest and disease resilience, without field data. A popular-science article claims natural resistance to pests and diseases without naming pathogens. The same ResearchGate source mentions strong resistance to an unnamed pest or disease, but the text is truncated and the target is unverified.
pest_resistance_summary: Shoot fly (Atherigona species) is the only pest named. The ResearchGate source describes DHLM-28-4 as shoot-fly resistant and reports a shoot-fly tolerance figure of 19.42%, but the source does not clarify the scoring basis and is a promotional page without field data. An ICAR/AICRP proceedings report gives the peak shoot-fly timing in small millets (second half of August screening window); it does not provide resistance data for DHLM-28-4.
drought_details_research: No drought trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. The only related evidence is species-level: little millet (Panicum sumatrense) as a species is reported to tolerate drought, salinity and waterlogging. This is not specific to DHLM-28-4 and cannot be attributed to the variety.
heat_details_research: No heat stress trial or evidence specific to DHLM-28-4 was found in the digest.
salinity_details_research: No salinity trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. Species-level reports indicate little millet tolerates salinity; this is not variety-specific.
flood_details_research: No flood trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. Species-level reports indicate little millet tolerates waterlogging; this is not variety-specific.

Parentage per CSC record is HJ 8 x Kent, but the release article does not give the cross parents, so this parentage is unverified. Heterosis studies used OS-377 as a female parent in crosses OS-377 x JHO-851 and OS-377 x PLP-1, which were flagged for earliness, seed yield, fodder yield and plant height.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: Release-article agronomic trials: OS-377 gave 522.1 q/ha green fodder yield, superior to national checks OS 6 (471.7 q/ha) and Kent (476.9 q/ha) and zonal check JHO 822 (479.6 q/ha). For dry matter yield, OS-377 (84.1 q/ha) was statistically at par with Kent (86.3 q/ha), OS 6 (85.7 q/ha) and JHO 822 (85.5 q/ha). CSC record (no URL): at Jhansi, OS-377 recorded the highest green fodder yield (688.7 q/ha) and dry matter yield (98.5 q/ha). Heterosis evaluation flagged OS-377 x JHO-851 and OS-377 x PLP-1 for earliness, seed yield, fodder yield and plant height.

agronomic_performance_adaptation: Recommended for Tamil Nadu. The release record describes benefit to onion growing regions of Tamil Nadu and other South Indian states (states not named in the digest). Review table lists CO-6 as suited to kharif and rabi seasons.

Dry pinkish scale leaves arranged compactly on bulbs and bulblets (IJCMAS 18939). Review table lists CO-6 as pink-bulbed. Breeding objective was a seed setting onion type with attractive pink bulbs (IJCMAS 18939).
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) TNAU ART over five years, Aca 15 vs check CO (On) 5: highest bulb yield 22.84 t/ha, 22.32 per cent increase over check; seed trials sent to 12 districts of Tamil Nadu. (3) TNAU good-practice table (secondary, not traced to primary trial): CO 6 average yield 19.10 t/ha. (4) Review table: CO-6 18.90 t/ha, association uncertain. (5) Savitha BK (2022-23 rabi study): Aca 15 listed among populations superior to the check; journal not captured.

The original variety data reports 38.23 per cent thrips incidence, classed as Moderately Susceptible. This conflicts with the digest evidence and is reported without resolution. The digest's Aca 15 thrips figure is treated as CO 6 evidence because the digest equates the two names.

agronomic_performance_yield: CSC data: 25000.00 to 30000.00 Kg/Ha. ICAR release notice: average multi-location yield 185 q/ha (18.5 t/ha) in recommended zones. Secondary page (asiafarming): mean yield about 19 t/ha in recommended zones. Kharif preprint: marketable yield 19.96 t/ha and total yield 26.22 t/ha, the lowest total yield in a nine-variety set. These values differ across sources and were not reconciled.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: CSC recommended states: Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu. CSC adaptation ecology text instead recommends Kharif release and cultivation in Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan and Gujarat; this conflicts with the recommended-states list and is reported as found. Kharif bulbs are also reported as stored for 30-45 days, and late kharif up to 3 months, per the DOGR listing. ICAR release notice describes white round to oval bulbs of 70-80 g, 11-12 percent TSS, suitable for table and processing.

agronomic_performance_yield: Frontline demonstrations in Madurai reported a 29.41% yield increase over traditional practice. Virudhunagar rabi farmer-field trials (2017-18 and 2018-19) reported 16.61% more yield than CO(KV)2. A review cites 2,500 kg/ha grain yield for MDU 1 (Vanniarajan et al., 2018, as cited). A 2023 Indian Farming entry gives 24.0 q/ha grain and 5.5-6.5 t/ha fodder, while a second entry gives 32.0 q/ha and 6-7 t/ha fodder. The two entries conflict and it is unclear which applies to MDU-1, so they are not used as a figure.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Rainfed kharif crop in the digest's agronomy entries. Frontline demonstrations were in Madurai (Thirumangalam, Usilampatti, Sedapatti blocks). Rabi trials were in Virudhunagar. Recommended state: Tamil Nadu. Digest reports bolder grains and about 70% milling recovery. Iron content of 16 mg/100 g grain and whitish grain with better cooking quality are reported. MDU-1 had the highest polyphenol, flavonoid, tannin and antioxidant contents among the barnyard millet varieties tested in a nutraceutical comparison.
agronomic_performance_maturity_days: 95-100 days in one report (sdbindex); 90-95 days in a second report (IARJSET). The two reports differ.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Frontline demonstrations in Madurai (Thirumangalam, Usilampatti, Sedapatti blocks): 29.41% yield increase over traditional practice. (2) Virudhunagar rabi trials at farmers' fields, 2017-18 and 2018-19: MDU-1 yielded 16.61% more than CO(KV)2. (3) Salinity field trial at ADAC&RI, kharif 2019: MDU-1 result not given in the digest. (4) Path/correlation study at ACRI Trichy using MDU 1 as a control: accessions IEc 350 and IEc 356 were higher yielding than MDU 1. (5) A Krishi Vigyan Kendra training-impact study in Madurai district is listed under publications and is not a yield trial.

genetics_and_qtl_breeding_method: Pureline selection from a local Tamil Nadu landrace. Mutagenesis work in MDU-1 is also reported: LD50 values were 16.19 mM (EMS) and 14.14 mM (sodium azide) in M1 seed, and a mutation breeding programme using EMS and sodium azide is cited (Karthikeyan, 2022). Mutant lines are a separate material and are not a breeding method for the released variety.

salinity_details_research: Salinity is a significant abiotic stress for rice, with various salt-tolerant varieties and landraces (e.g., BINA 8, BRRI dhan 55, CARI Dhan 5 from Pokkali) being developed or studied (RESULT_21, RESULT_22, RESULT_26, RESULT_27). However, no specific information regarding the salinity tolerance of BR-39 (or BR 34/BRRI dhan 34) was found in the provided search results.
flood_details_research: Flooding events are frequent, necessitating flood-tolerant rice varieties. Varieties like CR Dhan 500 and BRRI dhan76 exhibit flood or tidal flood tolerance (RESULT_31, RESULT_33, RESULT_34, RESULT_35). The Sub1 QTL is noted for its mega effect on flood tolerance (RESULT_36). No specific information regarding the flood tolerance of BR-39 (or BR 34/BRRI dhan 34) was found in the provided search results.
submergence_details_research: Submergence tolerance is a crucial trait in rice, with the gene SUB1 playing a significant role in enabling survival under full submergence for up to 14 days (RESULT_34, RESULT_36, RESULT_47). Varieties like CR Dhan 801 and CR Dhan 802 show submergence tolerance, sometimes combined with drought tolerance (RESULT_37, RESULT_49). Anaerobic germination tolerance and tolerance to submergence at seedling stages are also areas of research (RESULT_41, RESULT_43, RESULT_44, RESULT_46, RESULT_50). No specific information regarding the submergence tolerance of BR-39 (or BR 34/BRRI dhan 34) was found in the provided search results.

This name differs from Bahadur-Sub1 and the attribution should be confirmed. Sub1 varieties in Assam, including Bahadur-Sub1, showed a yield advantage of 1.0-1.2 t/ha over non-Sub1 counterparts in 2018-19 to 2022-23, including under non-flooded conditions. Sub1 introgressed lines showed no overall yield penalty under non-flooded conditions (general finding, not Bahadur-specific).

agronomic_performance_yield: Average yield of 7.2 t/ha, reported as 10.5% over IR 64, 9.3% over Krishna Hansa, 10.4% over local check and 17.7% over Gautam. Potential yield is listed as 5.6 t/ha (Odisha sheet and CRRI PDF) and as 7.8 t/ha on another CRRI snippet; these figures conflict and should be checked against the original minutes. A Sentinel Assam report gives a yield range of 3.5 to 5.6 t/ha.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Boro rice area and Boro season. Listed as cold tolerant by CRRI, while the Odisha sheet records abiotic stress as minimal stress (conflict noted). Included in the Assam Seed Sub-Committee list of NRRI varieties for Assam based on performance at the Gerua station. A Sentinel Assam report describes use for Ahu, Sali and Boro seasons with duration of 115 to 145 days, which conflicts with the 160-day duration in other sources.
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Semi-dwarf stature (about 90 cm), medium-slender grain. Grain-quality and cooking traits (volume expansion, elongation and similar) are reported by the NRRI table, with the variety among those showing higher values.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Released by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards after high yield under Boro conditions at the 45th AICRIP workshop (08.04.2010). (2) Average yield of 7.2 t/ha, 10.5% over IR 64, 9.3% over Krishna Hansa, 10.4% over local check, and 17.7% over Gautam. (3) Potential yield conflicts between 5.6 t/ha and 7.8 t/ha across sources. (4) NRRI table reports higher values for grain-quality and cooking traits. (5) Assam Seed Sub-Committee included the variety in its NRRI list for Assam based on performance at the Gerua station. heat_details_research: This hybrid is identified as heat tolerant in nature and is suitable for yield enhancement under heat stress conditions. It has also shown a significant yield advantage in trials aimed at identifying heat-tolerant rice genotypes.
salinity_details_research: DRH 775 is listed among rice hybrids tolerant to abiotic stress conditions, which includes salinity. One source explicitly mentions it in the context of drought and salt tolerance in rice research.
flood_details_research: It exhibits tolerance to water logging and is listed among varieties tolerant to flash floods and stagnant flooding conditions, particularly relevant for direct-seeded rice (DSR).
submergence_details_research: DRH 775 is cited as a variety with submergence tolerance, and is suitable for semi-deep water conditions with reported tolerance for up to one week of submergence.

agronomic_performance_yield: Mean grain yield of 5030 kg/ha across the five states, which is 32%, 28%, 22% and 11% above the national, zonal, local and hybrid checks respectively. State-wise weighted mean yield was 5306 kg/ha, 14% above the best check. Up to 5.5-6.0 t/ha is reported under suitable conditions.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Released for aerobic (direct-seeded, water-limited) ecosystems. Evaluated and recommended for Punjab, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Tripura and Gujarat.
agronomic_performance_maturity_days: About 120 days seed to seed. Another copy of the paper gives 115-120 days versus transplanted rice.
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Grain and milling quality: hulling 79.2%, milling 71.3%, head rice recovery 62.8%. Long bold grain with KL 6.5 mm and KB 2.4 mm. Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: DRRH-4 was evaluated in AICRIP multi-location aerobic trials in wet seasons 2018 to 2021 and nominated in the AICRIP aerobic trial of 2018. Mean grain yield across the five states was 5030 kg/ha, with 32%, 28%, 22% and 11% advantages over national, zonal, local and hybrid checks. The state-wise weighted mean was 5306 kg/ha, 14% above the best check, across Punjab, Odisha, Tripura, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat. Trial results for other varieties (DRR Dhan 44) were excluded.

disease_resistance_summary: Moderately resistant to sheath blight and bacterial leaf blight (KAU varieties-released table). A Kaipad farm-level observation reported no pest or disease incidence under Kaipad field conditions; this is not a formal resistance rating and applies only to the described field condition.
pest_resistance_summary: Resistant to gall midge, leaf folder and case worm; moderately resistant to whorl maggot (KAU varieties-released table). Farm-level Kaipad observation reported no pest incidence under Kaipad field conditions; not a formal rating.
drought_details_research: No drought tolerance rating found. The Kaipad review describes the variety as suited to flood-prone and water-scarce environments, but this is an adaptation statement, not a tested drought-tolerance result. No drought mechanisms were reported.
salinity_details_research: KAU varieties-released table states tolerance of medium salinity. The variety was designed for saline-prone Kaipad fields and is described as saline-tolerant in the Kaipad review. It is reported as suited to coastal saline and flooded areas. In a hydroponic NaCl seedling study of ten rice varieties (Ezhome-1 and Ezhome-2 from KAU Trissur), low Na+/K+ ratio and antioxidant activity were linked to tolerance; this study is included under the Ezhome-1 name in the digest. Landraces used as salinity donors in the breeding programme were reported to differ in salinity tolerance mechanism (molecular evidence). The digest notes that the Pokkali-differing mechanism applies to Ezhome-2 and is excluded here.
flood_details_research: KAU varieties-released table lists tolerance of flooding. The Kaipad review describes suitability for flood-prone environments. The Journal of Organics paper reports suitability for flooded areas. No degree of flood tolerance (e.g., duration of submergence or yield under flood) was found.

heat_details_research: The variety exhibits tolerance to high temperature stress. Molecular markers have been validated for its high temperature stress tolerance, indicating advanced breeding for this trait.
salinity_details_research: Kalinga Dhan- 1301 is identified as salinity tolerant and has shown tolerance to osmotic stresses.
flood_details_research: While specific 'flood' tolerance is not explicitly stated, the variety exhibits robust submergence tolerance, which provides resilience against temporary waterlogging or inundation events.
submergence_details_research: This variety demonstrates one week submergence tolerance and is suitable for semi-deep water conditions. It has been actively screened for submergence tolerance in multi-location trials.

agronomic_performance_yield: AAU listing: 5-5.5 t/ha. On-farm trials: about 100% more yield than the local check. Morigaon demonstrations (2020-21, 157 ha, 430 farmers): pooled yield 20.04% higher than farmers' varieties. Lakhimpur (2018-19 and 2019-20): benefit-cost ratio 1.58 and 1.54 versus 1.31 and 1.35 for the farmers' variety; net returns Rs 24,460 and Rs 24,600 versus Rs 9,700 and Rs 10,698. submergence_details_research: Sub1 QTL introgression confers complete-submergence tolerance. agronomic_performance_yield: Seven-year trial mean of 6623 kg/ha, a 10.72% increase over ADT 43. Over 7000 kg/ha at 38 of 127 locations in 2010-11 and 2011-12. The original variety data gives average_yield as Kg/Ha with no value.
agronomic_performance_stability: Yield tested at 127 locations across 17 districts in 2010-11 and 2011-12. Stability indices across environments were not found in searched sources.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Irrigated condition, transplanted crop in Sornavari, Kar, Kuruvai and Navarai seasons of Tamil Nadu. Recommended for kharif, rabi and summer in Tamil Nadu per the digest. Suitable for Kuruvai season per Tamil Nadu advisory. Recommended states are listed in the variety profile.
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Semi-dwarf high-yielding habit (release description). Non-lodging and non-shattering (original variety data). Seed rate 20 kg/ha under normal conditions and 5 kg/ha under SRI. Seedling age 22-25 days under normal conditions and 14-15 days under SRI. Milling 69% and head rice recovery 63% at release. Good milling quality. Morphological characteristics otherwise not specified.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Yield trials at 127 locations across 17 districts in 2010-11 and 2011-12; over 7000 kg/ha at 38 locations. (2) Seven-year trial mean of 6623 kg/ha, 10.72% above ADT 43. (3) SRI trial at Coimbatore, Kharif 2010-11 (from original variety data, no URL supplied): higher yield under SRI than normal method; agronomic efficiency 37.2% normal and 48.3% SRI versus check ADT 3 at 30.5% normal and 33.5% SRI; higher crop growth rate, leaf area index, light transmission ratio, spikelet fertility, dry matter production and harvest index. (4) Three-year pest evaluation (2009-2011) at Coimbatore, Madurai and Aduthurai. (5) Artificial inoculation disease screening in 2009, 2010 and 2011. (6) AICRIP screening in 2010 and NSN-1 and DSN-1 entries. (7) Heat-stress flowering assessment reported in the MDPI 2023 study. Socio-economic survey of CO 51 growers in Kancheepuram and Tiruvarur districts (150 farmers per district) is not a yield trial.
genetics_and_qtl_qtl_information: qEMF3 (early morning flowering) introgressed by marker-assisted backcrossing with CO 51 as recurrent parent. Backcross lines reduced heat-induced sterility by about 8.15% in the CO 51 background. QTL effect size beyond this value was not reported.
genetics_and_qtl_molecular_mechanisms: Early morning flowering (qEMF3) shifts flowering away from the hottest part of the day to reduce heat-induced spikelet sterility. Resistance to blast (Pi54, Pi9), bacterial blight (xa13, Xa21) and gall midge (Gm1, Gm4) relies on single resistance genes; no pathway-level mechanism was reported.
genetics_and_qtl_genes_introgressed: Pi54 (native to CO 51). Introduced by marker-assisted introgression: Pi9, xa13, Xa21, Gm1, Gm4 (the donor line named in the digest is 562-4, used in the CO 51 x 562-4 F6 and BC2F6 progenies; the donor of each individual gene was not stated). qEMF3 donor not stated.
genetics_and_qtl_parentage_and_pedigree: ADT 43 / RR 272-1745 (as published in the release paper). A pedigree chart is published in the release paper.

disease_resistance_summary: Blast: moderately resistant (score 5 on 1-9 scale) under artificial inoculation in 2009, 2010 and 2011; ADT 43 scored 7 or 9. Under AICRIP, moderately resistant to blast in NSN-1 and DSN-1. Pi54 is native; Pi9 stacked onto CO 51 plus Pi54 gave a blast score of 0-2 (strong resistance). Bacterial blight: genes xa13 and Xa21 were introgressed through marker-assisted selection, but no bacterial blight score was reported in the digest. Sheath rot, sheath blight, brown spot and rice tungro disease (RTD) were screened in 2009-2011 but no reaction scores were reported in the digest. Release reports better disease resistance than check ADT 43.
pest_resistance_summary: Green leafhopper (GLH): moderately resistant (score 5) in three years of evaluation (2009-2011) at Coimbatore, Madurai and Aduthurai. Brown planthopper (BPH): moderately resistant (score 3). Under AICRIP (2010), moderately resistant to white-backed planthopper (WBPH), leaf folder and stem borer. Gall midge: resistance is targeted by the Gm1 and Gm4 introgression, but no reaction score was reported in the digest. Release reports better pest resistance than check ADT 43.
heat_details_research: The variety is reported as extremely susceptible to high temperature because of late morning flowering, which causes heat-induced spikelet sterility. A marker-assisted early-morning-flowering (qEMF3) backcross version of CO 51 reduced heat-induced sterility by about 8.15% in the CO 51 background. This indicates the parent CO 51 is heat-sensitive and the EMF version is a mitigation attempt, not evidence of tolerance.

disease_resistance_summary: Bacterial blight (BB): the variety itself is reported as highly susceptible to BB and blast (PLoS ONE 2020). Marker-assisted backcrossing introgressed xa13 and Xa21 (BB) and Pi54 and Pi1 (blast) into Tellahamsa; two ICF3 pyramided lines, TH-625-159 and TH-625-491, showed high resistance, but these are breeding derivatives and not the released variety. Blast response of the four-, three- and two-gene pyramided lines varied. Resistance at the level of the released variety is therefore not established; the reported high susceptibility is the only release-level disease finding.

agronomic_performance_yield: Average grain yield 2589 kg/ha, 3.5 per cent higher than check hybrid GHB 538. Dry fodder yield 6320 kg/ha, 10.8 per cent higher than check hybrid GHB 538. CSC record lists average yield as 8.0 to 11.5 quintals per acre (Kg/Ha); the digest does not independently verify this range.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Recommended to Gujarat kharif growers as a downy mildew resistant and early maturing hybrid. Original hybrid recommended for scanty rainfall areas of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Haryana (A-1 Zone). Original hybrid sowing advice for North Saurashtra: first week of October.
agronomic_performance_maturity_days: Improved hybrid: early flowering at 44 days (state testing) and 45 days (AICRP testing), per the digest. Original hybrid: maturity group 71-76 days in summer and pre-rabi season and 65-70 days in kharif season. Total maturity days for the improved hybrid not specified in the digest.
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Original hybrid: medium tall, good tillering, drought resistant, matures within 65-70 days. Improved hybrid morphological characteristics not captured in the digest.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Yield trials against the original GHB-538 at Jamnagar and other substations, 2018 to 2020, kharif season: result reported as 3.5% higher grain yield and 10.8% higher dry fodder yield than check hybrid GHB 538 (2589 kg/ha grain; 6320 kg/ha dry fodder). (2) State testing: early flowering at 44 days. (3) AICRP on Pearl Millet A1 zone trials under testing code MH 2661: early flowering at 45 days. (4) Downy mildew screening under DM sick plot at different locations of Gujarat, with the 82.0% downy mildew resistance figure reported. Trial-level replication, plot design and statistical significance were not captured in the digest.
genetics_and_qtl_genetic_markers: Marker-assisted backcross with foreground selection was used. QTL positions reported: the P7-3-P13 donor contributed an LG3 QTL; the donor and 863B-P2-P7 contributed LG1 and LG4 QTLs (the digest does not fully disambiguate which donor carried LG1 and LG4). No SSR or SNP marker names were captured in the digest.
genetics_and_qtl_qtl_information: Downy mildew resistance QTLs introgressed from P7-3-P13 and 863B-P2-P7 into the pollen parent J-2340 of the earlier released GHB-538. Introgression lines were at BC3F5 and were crossed to form a QTL heterozygote. Effect sizes not captured in the digest. The CSC parentage (ICMR 11009 and ICMR 11019 lines with R-line pedigree) was not found in any retrieved source and was not verified. Original parentage per JAU release dossier: ICMA 95444A x J-2340 (seed parent ICMA 95444A; pollinator J-2340).

disease_resistance_summary: Improved hybrid (Maru Sona): high resistance to downy mildew (82.0%) described as markedly higher than the original hybrid; resistance to blast (28.6%) and rust (91.4%) reported; grain yield increase of 3.5% and fodder yield increase of 10.8% over the check hybrid GHB 538. Downy mildew screening was conducted under the DM sick plot at different locations of Gujarat. The original hybrid was overcome by downy mildew within five years of release, which motivated the improvement. Original hybrid is listed as resistant to downy mildew, smut, ergot, blast and rust in the JAU release dossier. Percentages are as reported in the sources; the digest does not state the measurement method.

These statements describe the original hybrid, not the improved version. Mechanisms not described in the digest.

(3) AICRP 2015-16 advance trial: check grain yield 3421 kg/ha at 78 days, downy mildew 1.2% at 60 DAS. (4) Rainfed FLDs, Jodhpur, kharif 2022-23: grain 1.03-1.18 t/ha versus 0.67-0.76 t/ha for farmers' practice. Irrigated FLDs: 1.24-1.37 t/ha versus 0.78-0.93 t/ha. (5) Farmers FIRST, Rajasthan (2017): 20.6 q/ha seed under rainfed conditions, 18.4% over local; straw 20% higher; additional net return about Rs 6,500/ha. (6) Jaipur district (Devla and Jharna), rainfed, 10 farmers: higher grain and fodder than local practice. (7) Grain biofortification trial: HHB 299 out-yielded MPMH 17 under irrigation in Zone A (24.73 vs 21.31 q/ha) and Zone B (27.14 vs 24.77 q/ha); MPMH 17 had higher Mn. (8) Zinc fertilization, Jobner (2019-20): MPMH 17 had lower crude protein than RHB-173. (9) Customized fertilizer trial, Mandor (2019-20): plant height about 192.6 cm; yield response reported with other hybrids, no MPMH 17-specific yield value given. (10) Heterosis study, Mandor 2019: MPMH 17 used as the check; no result for MPMH 17 itself given.

agronomic_performance_yield: Quantitative yield is not specified. However, Punjab-89 has been observed to record the highest number of branches per plant in performance studies in the North-Western Himalayan Region, which may correlate with higher yield potential. It is noted that the legumes give 55% seeds.
agronomic_performance_stability: It has been evaluated under both irrigated and rainfed conditions, suggesting adaptability to varying moisture availability. Its suitability for different seasons implies environmental stability.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Well-adapted for cultivation in Punjab, being developed by PAU. It has been evaluated in the foothills of the Terai Agro-ecological Region of West Bengal, the North-Western Himalayan Region, and Bihar. It is suited for different seasons and can be grown as a winter crop. While generally adaptable to various soil types, alkaline soils with high salt concentration are not suitable for pea cultivation. It cannot tolerate frost.
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Medium dwarf, vigorous plants with a pant height of 92 cm. It produces a high number (28-30) of well-filled pods per plant. The pods are dark green and long, typically containing 9-10 wrinkle seeds.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: Field trials have been conducted in West Bengal under irrigated and rainfed conditions. Performance studies were also carried out in the North-Western Himalayan Region. It was also used in field testing for PGPR strains and in randomized block designs for cultivation studies, including optimal sowing dates (e.g., November 5th) and spacing (20 x 7.5 cm).
genetics_and_qtl_genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (QTL, SNP, SSR) are detailed for Punjab-89 in the provided results. General pea QTLs for heat stress tolerance are mentioned but not linked directly to this variety.
genetics_and_qtl_qtl_information: No specific QTLs identified for Punjab-89. General research on QTLs for heat stress tolerance in pea is noted.
genetics_and_qtl_molecular_mechanisms: Punjab-89 has been used in field testing to understand the molecular mechanisms of Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) strains in promoting plant growth under abiotic stress conditions, including salt stress.

disease_resistance_summary: Punjab-89 is resistant to rust and tolerant to powdery mildew and wilt. It has been studied in the context of gene-based resistance to Erysiphe species causing powdery mildew.
drought_details_research: Recognized as a drought-resistant vegetable. Evaluation under irrigated and rainfed conditions in West Bengal indicated it could be selected as drought-tolerant, exhibiting a high drought tolerance index. Water stress should be avoided during flowering and seed formation for the crop in general.
heat_details_research: Studies have explored heat stress tolerance in peas, and Punjab-89 has been noted in contexts related to developing varieties with terminal heat tolerance. It is suited for different seasons, but peas generally are cool-weather crops.
salinity_details_research: It is mentioned as tolerant to salt stress, particularly when field tested with PGPR (Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria) strains like Priestia megaterium IHB B 7164, which promotes plant growth under stress conditions including salt. It is also listed among varieties classified as resistant or tolerant to salt conditions, and suitable for main season cultivation in areas affected by saline lands.
flood_details_research: It has shown some ability to germinate under anaerobic conditions.
submergence_details_research: No specific information on submergence tolerance beyond anaerobic germination.

A study titled 'Performance and economic impact of Pigeaon pea-(BDN-711) under drought condition' reports that BDN 711 performed well under drought conditions in a NICRA village in Marathwada, Maharashtra. The full study text was not retrieved, so the level rests on the escape mechanism and the summary of that study, not on quantitative yield data. Escape is not the same as tolerance, so the level reflects the evidence available, not a measured tolerance score.

In KVK Mudigere frontline demonstrations (kharif 2016-17 to 2018-19, rainfed hill zone), yield ranged from 50.5 to 60.5 q/ha, averaging 55.73 q/ha versus 44.67 q/ha under farmer practice. agronomic_performance_yield: Seed yield on par with the national check A-1 (NARI AR2015). AICRP table lists yield about 1500 kg/ha. CSC record gives average_yield as 'Kg/Ha' with no numeric value. Oil yield 18.36% higher than A-1 in coordinated trials over locations and years (AR2015).
agronomic_performance_stability: Per the CSC record, performance is at par with check A-1 for sowing under different dates and under varied nutrient conditions. Oil yield advantage over A-1 is reported across locations and years in coordinated trials (AR2015). Responsive to fertilizer and time of sowing (CSC record). Non-lodging and non-shattering (CSC record).
agronomic_performance_adaptation: CSC record: safflower growing areas of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and West Bengal. Recommended for timely sowing with normal spacing (seed rate). Sowing-date trial in 2014-15 used an October 24, 2014 first sowing date, with first-date sowing giving higher oil content than the other two dates.
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Non-lodging, non-shattering, responsive to fertilizer and time of sowing, recommended for timely sowing with normal spacing (CSC record). Produces brilliant orange flowers at bloom (AR2015). Morphological characteristics not specified in CSC record.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Seed yield in coordinated trials: on par with national check A-1 (AR2015). (2) Oil yield in coordinated trials over locations and years: 18.36% higher than A-1 (AR2015). (3) 2014-15 sowing trial, first sowing date October 24, 2014: oil content 36.37% for NARI-57, versus 27.97% for A-1 and 31.65% for NARI-6, the highest oil content recorded in that trial (AR2015). (4) Sowing-date effect: first date of sowing recorded higher oil content than the remaining two dates (AR2015). (5) 2015-16 varietal trial: NARI-57 gave the significantly highest oil among varieties tested (AR2016). (6) AICRP table: yield about 1500 kg/ha, days to maturity 118-151, oil 29%. Discrepancy: oil content figures conflict across sources: 36.6% (AR2015 average), 38% (NARI R&D summary), 37 (NARI release table), and 29% (AICRP success stories). These are reported as a discrepancy and not resolved.

No independent source in the digest confirms this. None of the retrieved pages reported rust, smut, blight or other disease reaction for GW-322.
drought_details_research: The digest found no independent evidence for drought tolerance of GW-322. The CSC record states that GW 322 gave its highest yield under late sowing and with one, two and three irrigations, which the record interprets as tolerance to terminal heat and drought. This is a record statement and is not corroborated by any retrieved source. Source for the drought claim: CSC record (no URL).
heat_details_research: The digest found no evidence for heat tolerance of GW-322 itself. The only heat-related result (Wheat & Barley Newsletter) concerns DBW 150, a different line derived from a DBW 16/GW 322 cross, and was deliberately not attributed to GW-322. The CSC record's terminal-heat interpretation (highest yield under late sowing) is uncorroborated.

agronomic_performance_adaptation: Submitted record: recommended for normal sown, high fertility, irrigated conditions of the entire Northern Plains Zone, and suitable for early to medium sown conditions. agronomic_performance_field_trials: One study examined PBW-34 grain yield under poplar (Populus deltoides) plantations in Punjab, India. Under six-year-old poplar plantations, PBW-34 showed a 57.1% grain yield reduction, compared with 19.4% for PBW-222 and 15.3% for HD-2329. Yield reduction was measured relative to open-field yield. The trial design and year are not visible in the retrieved text. No multi-location or other field-trial results for PBW-34 were found.

A 2018-2023 compendium of notified Indian wheat varieties lists "PBW34" as a parent of the durum line DDW 47. This is a pedigree reference only and is not evidence about PBW-34's own genetics.

Glutenin-based clustering placed Kundan-DL-153-2 in cluster I with UP-2338, HD-2329 and others. Positions not stated.

The donor for any introgressed gene was not stated.

disease_resistance_summary: Stem rust (Puccinia graminis): Kundan is described as Ug99-resistant and was screened against Indian stem rust pathotypes 40A (62G29) and 122 (7G11). Stem rust resistance was studied in F2 populations (Kundan x UP 2338; UP 2338 x Agra Local), which segregated 3:1 resistant:susceptible. Kundan's specific Sr gene status (Sr22, Sr24, Sr26, Sr31, Sr39 marker screen) was not resolved in the extracted text. Leaf rust, yellow rust, Karnal bunt and powdery mildew: the CSC variety record reports resistance to all four, but none of these was corroborated by the searched sources. The digest found no yellow rust evidence and reports this as a conflict to be checked against the official record. Leaf blight: no evidence found.
pest_resistance_summary: The CSC variety record states that no insect attack has ever been observed on DL 153-2 and that the variety is free from storage pests, possibly because of the very hard seed texture typical of deshi wheats. The searched sources found no insect evidence. This claim rests on the CSC record only and has no supporting URL.
drought_details_research: No drought evidence was found in the searched sources. Kundan's inclusion in a fertility-gradient stability trial is not a drought test.

The rating is comparative only. A separate NDUAT Narendra Nagar elevated-temperature study included Kundan, but no tolerance rating for Kundan was extracted.

agronomic_performance_yield: Yield potential per CSSRI: 4.0 t/ha in normal soils and 3.0 t/ha in sodic soils (pH up to 9.3). A conflicting figure on the same page gives 5.2 t/ha in normal soils and 3.5 t/ha in salt-affected soils (pH up to 9.3, EC up to 6 dS/m). The original variety record gives an average yield of 4100 to 4900 kg/ha.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Recommended for salt-affected soils of the North West Plain Zone (NWPZ) and North East Plain Zone (NEPZ). Suitable for timely sown conditions. Germination is delayed under salt stress, so timely sowing is essential. Seed rate of 125 kg/ha is advised for salt-affected soils.
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Dwarf type with 145 days to maturity. Hard, medium-bold, amber grain. Quality: about 11% protein, 77 kg/hl test weight, sedimentation value 29. Non-lodging and non-shattering per original variety record.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) ICAR-IARI Water Technology Centre, New Delhi: field trials under saline irrigation of 1.7 to 12 dS/m reported water-productivity gains with foliar potassium for KRL-1-4. (2) Rabi 2012-13: grain yield increase of 4.5 to 20% over control (source reports rabi 2011-12 and 2012-13 evaluations of different cultivars under salinity stress). (3) Multi-site Indian field study of grain Zn and ionome (2013-14 and 2014-15): KRL 1-4 is one of 36 genotypes; no yield result for KRL 1-4 was reported in the digest. (4) Pot study (not a field trial): proline and reducing sugars rose most strongly with salinity in KRL 1-4 compared with UP 2338. (5) Farmer demonstrations on alkali soils with other CSSRI wheat lines are reported; the page gives no KRL 1-4 yields.
genetics_and_qtl_qtl_information: Parent-level salinity QTL (Nax1/Nax2 in Kharchia 65) are documented in the digest, but the source does not name KRL 1-4, so they are not attributed to this variety. QTL/marker study on KRL 1-4 itself: No evidence found.
genetics_and_qtl_parentage_and_pedigree: Kharchia 65 x WL 711. Kharchia 65 is described as the most salt-tolerant wheat variety from Rajasthan, derived from Kharchia Local x EG 953. WL 711 is described as a well-adapted, high-yielding Punjab variety derived from (S. 308 x Chris) x Kalyan Sona. A review also gives the cross as Kharchia 65 and WL 711 and calls it promising for northern India. The review states that all Indian salt-tolerant cultivars, including KRL 1-4, are progeny of Kharchia 65.

salinity_details_research: Bred for salt tolerance to ECe 6.0 dS/m in saline soils and to pH 9.2 in alkaline soils (CSSRI states it was bred for both conditions). Sodicity tolerance is listed as up to pH 9.3 with salinity tolerance of 7.0 dS/m. Germination is unaffected up to pH 9.4 if sown under proper moisture conditions (original variety record; not an independent digest finding). A pot study reported that proline and reducing sugars rose with salinity most strongly in KRL 1-4, which the study classes as the tolerant cultivar (compared with UP 2338). agronomic_performance_yield: Under rainfed conditions, average grain yield was 2117 kg/ha and straw yield 2785 kg/ha, representing 9.6% (grain) and 14.8% (straw) increases over the check CO (Te) 7. Per plant grain yield was 20.8% higher than CO (Te) 7. Note: the ground-truth average_yield field (2785 kg/ha) matches the straw yield value in the digest, not the grain yield; this discrepancy is unresolved.

agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Digest reports synchronous flowering and uniform maturity, non-lodging and non-shattering habit, and easy threshability. Quality: protein 12.3%, mineral matter 3.5%, calcium 34 mg/100 g and iron 5.7 mg/100 g, the highest among compared varieties including CO (Te) 7. Apical sterility is absent in ATL 1 and present in CO (Te) 7. Ground-truth record also lists strong culm, stay-green leaves, and positive response to nitrogenous fertilizers.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: Rainfed trial: grain yield 2117 kg/ha and straw yield 2785 kg/ha, 9.6% (grain) and 14.8% (straw) above check CO (Te) 7. Per plant grain yield 20.8% above CO (Te) 7. Grain quality analysis: highest protein (12.3%), mineral matter (3.5%), calcium (34 mg/100 g) and iron (5.7 mg/100 g) versus CO (Te) 7 and other checks. Multi-location or AICRP trials: No evidence found.

agronomic_performance_yield: Ground-truth data: grain 1587 kg/ha, straw 3109 kg/ha. Station trial: 1859 kg grain and 3633 kg straw/ha. Multi-location: 1343 kg grain and 2616 kg straw/ha. Large-scale demonstration: 2223 kg grain and 4106 kg straw/ha. Station average of 1966 kg/ha for TNPsu 177 with a 21.60% increase (TNPsu 176 averaged 1859 kg/ha with a 15.00% increase). Yield advantage over checks CO(Samai) 4 and Paiyur 2: 11.2% and 13.7% for grain, and 11.8% to 14.4% for straw.
agronomic_performance_stability: Multi-location yield (1343 kg grain/ha) was lower than station yield (1859 kg/ha) and large-scale demonstration yield (2223 kg/ha). Stability across environments is not otherwise quantified in the digest.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Highly suitable for Eastern Ghats districts Dharmapuri, Tiruvannamalai, Vellore, Salem and Krishnagiri. Very much adaptive in the plains under rainfed systems. Suitable for both early and late sown conditions; if early sown, a second crop of horsegram or niger can be sown in the sequence.
agronomic_performance_plant_characterist: Plant height 103.78 cm compared with 91.8 cm for CO 4. Short duration. Synchronous flowering and uniform maturity. Non-lodging and non-shattering. Strong culm and stay-green leaves. Long, semi-compact panicles. Positive response to nitrogenous fertilizer. Suitable for mechanical harvesting. Seed rate: 10 kg/ha for line sowing, 12.5 kg/ha for broadcasting. Nutrient-rich grains with high milling recovery; palatable and nutritious straw. Morphological descriptor data is not available in the digest.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: Station trials: TNPsu 177 averaged 1966 kg/ha, a 21.60% increase over the check, and was promoted for MLT testing. Proposal summary: station 1859 kg grain and 3633 kg straw/ha; multi-location 1343 and 2616 kg/ha; large-scale demonstration 2223 and 4106 kg/ha. Advantage over checks CO(Samai) 4 and Paiyur 2 was 11.2% and 13.7% for grain and 11.8% to 14.4% for straw. AICRP 2022-23 used ATL 1 as a check at CEM Athiyandal. Trial data for disease and pest screening was not found.

pest_resistance_summary: Bud fly (Dasyneura lini): the CSC record states the variety is early in flowering and maturity and escapes bud fly attack. Digest evidence contradicts this. The CSC record and a Scribd OSPS-13 booklet state the variety 'withstands moisture stress' and is suited to rainfed land. This is unverified (the Scribd source is not confirmed as ICAR) and is not equivalent to a drought tolerance rating.
salinity_details_research: Used as the salt-tolerant check in a multi-environment salinity study. Seed yield per plant was 6.34 g with a salt tolerance index of 0.81, compared with 1.01 to 1.63 for the 15 best accessions tested against it. The variety is therefore a reference standard, and its index is below the top-performing accessions. The level is an interpretation of this comparison, not a direct rating.

agronomic_performance_yield: About 1500 kg/ha (DOD variety table; trade listing, non-official). AICRP success stories give 1500-1600 kg/ha (All India). CSC record gives 1500.00 to 1600.00 kg/ha. In the rainfed Vertisol trial, seed yields were lower than spiny checks.
agronomic_performance_stability: Non-spiny group seed yield was about 50% below spiny cultivars (digest source). No multi-environment stability analysis for PBNS-40 was found.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Recommended for release and cultivation in safflower-growing areas under irrigated and rainfed conditions (CSC record). Advisory bulletin for Marathwada (October 2017) lists PBNS-40 among varieties to select for the rabi season. Responsive to 1-2 irrigations (CSC record).
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Rainfed Vertisol trial over 3 seasons (2009/10-2011/12): 100-seed weight 4.1 g and maturity 118-128 days; seed yields lower than spiny checks. (2) Reduced soil moisture study at three depths: PBNS-40 had the lowest oil concentration (about 20%) and oil yield (about 94 kg/ha) among the non-spiny and spiny cultivars tested. (3) Non-spiny group, including PBNS-40, had seed yield about 50% below spiny cultivars. (4) DOD variety table and AICRP success stories report yield of about 1500 kg/ha (AICRP range 1500-1600 kg/ha) and oil about 27%. (5) Insecticide field study on safflower aphid used PBNS-40 as the test cultivar; no outcome for PBNS-40 was confirmed.
genetics_and_qtl_genetic_markers: RAPD markers were used to assess genetic similarity among parental lines, and PBNS-40 is one of the parental genotypes in that cluster analysis. No marker names, positions or SNP/SSR details were found.

The original CSC record gives a drought tolerance efficiency of 81.2 under normal plant density conditions; this value is from the input record, not from the digest, and no mechanisms were identified in the digest.

disease_resistance_summary: CSC variety record: PA-255 showed reaction similar to PA-183 for bacterial blight, grey mildew (powdery mildew) and Alternaria leaf spot, and was moderately resistant to anthracnose. The CSC record has no URL in the digest. The VNMKV listing states PA-255 is among varieties released with tolerance to pests and diseases, but names no specific pathogen. No pathogen-specific resistance data beyond the CSC record was found. The level for each disease is not assigned because the digest gives no quantitative scoring.
pest_resistance_summary: Conflicting evidence. (1) The VNMKV listing and the DAC document cite general pest tolerance for desi cotton and PA-255. (2) A krishikosh genetic-transformation thesis states this desi cultivar is susceptible to all lepidopteran insects. This conflicts with the pest-tolerance claims and is not reconciled in the digest. (3) An Earias vitella biology study found larvae developed more suitably on PA-255 than on NHH-44 or Paras Brahma, which indicates host suitability rather than resistance. (4) The DAC document reports Bt genes (Cry1Ac, Cry1Aa3) transferred into PA 255. No verified lepidopteran resistance level is established.
drought_details_research: The CSC variety record describes PA-255 as tolerant to drought compared with PA-183 and suitable for rainfed cultivation after onset of monsoon. The DAC document describes the variety as having tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses for rainfed cotton. The Marathwada adoption study recommends PA 255 for assured-rainfall areas. No quantitative drought-screening result naming PA-255 was found. A Parbhani drought-screening study of 12 genotypes was reviewed, but its snippet does not name PA-255 in the results, so it is not recorded as a finding. The level is medium because the evidence is relative to PA-183 and not quantified.

The sources conflict in direction at the germination stage, and no physiological mechanism is described for this variety. The medium level reflects the tolerance claim tempered by the germination finding. Cold tolerance is also listed on the BCKV page but is outside the requested stress categories.

The user-supplied record's wording on waterlogging is not web-verified and is not counted as evidence.

agronomic_performance_yield: Digest findings: (1) Organic and inorganic nutrient trial at RARS Lam, kharif 2003-04 and 2004-05, vertisols: the best treatment (green manure, neem cake, Azospirillum, PSB, burnt ash with 100% recommended N) gave 5397 kg/ha dry chilli. (2) Western Ghats multi-genotype thrips evaluation: LCA-334 gave the highest mean yield (133 q/ha), on par with RHRCH-10-2 (126.4 q/ha). Variety data record (CSC ground truth, not digest): average yield under normal conditions 1490 KG/KH (dry chilli), unit as printed; the record's average_yield field reads 'Unknown'. Digest comparator: ICAR release table lists LCA-334 as the control for later Lam releases, which claim 20-35% yield advantages over it.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: Digest: Konkan (coastal Maharashtra) trial judged LCA-334 suitable for the Konkan region. Variety data record (CSC ground truth): recommended for release and cultivation in Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Punjab, Orissa (Odisha), Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh; medium maturity. Agronomic features from the record: responds well to 200 kg N, 50 kg P2O5 and 80 kg K2O per ha; seed rate 2.0 to 2.5 kg/acre (650 g/acre); spacing rainfed 650 x 15 cm, irrigated 60 x 30 cm or 60 x 60 cm; oleoresin 10.0-10.6%, capsanthin 20618 to 22082 EOA units, capsaicin 0.450 to 0.618%.

agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Organic and inorganic nutrient management trial, RARS Lam, kharif 2003-04 and 2004-05, vertisols: best treatment gave 5397 kg/ha dry chilli (100% recommended N with organic amendments). (2) Salinity screen of 20 genotypes: LCA 334 highly sensitive to saline conditions. (3) Thrips tolerance evaluation, rabi 2022-23, Western Ghats agro-climatic region: LCA-334 gave the highest mean yield (133 q/ha), on par with RHRCH-10-2 (126.4 q/ha); thrips score not reported in snippet. (5) Drying-method and chemical-treatment trial, Lam, 2003-04: method and chemical treatment effects on oleoresin, capsanthin and capsaicin were found; no numeric values in the digest. (6) Diallel evaluation (2013-14) of six parents and F1 hybrids for yield traits, including LCA 334; crosses selected on yield-trait performance. (7) Fruit rot and die-back data from the Lam trial relate to nutrient treatments and are not counted as variety-level evidence.

agronomic_performance_stability: The ARI 2018-19 report describes stable, high yields in Central Zone trials. The CSC record states the variety ranked first in mean performance over three years at different Central Zone locations in coordinated trials.
agronomic_performance_adaptation: The ARI research page states the variety was identified for cultivation in the Central Zone of India. The CSC record lists adaptation as the Bundelkhand region of UP. The user-supplied recommended-state list is given in the variety profile.
agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) ARI 2016-17 annual report: significantly highest yield in an Initial Varietal Trial at Hol Farm. (2) ARI 2018-19 annual report: 17% higher yield than check DSB 21 (2308 kg/ha) and first rank over three years of Central Zone yield trials. (3) Soybean technology brochure: about 2200 kg/ha yield, about 97 days to maturity, good plant height for mechanical harvest, purple flowers with black hilum. (4) MACS 1407 paper: MACS 1520 included in a summer seed-production comparison, but the abstract is ambiguous and no firm result is recorded. (5) Drought and whitefly studies are not yield trials and are not used for yield. (6) Agronomic features in the CSC record (lodging resistance from thick stem, pod non-shattering up to ten days after maturity, 45 cm row spacing with 5-7 cm plant spacing, seed rate 65-70 kg/ha) are not verified by the retrieved sources.

disease_resistance_summary: Source of disease ratings: CSC/original variety record (not confirmed by retrieved sources). Charcoal rot: Absolute Resistance (AR) at Jabalpur, Sehore and Amravati. Yellow mosaic virus (YMV): susceptible. Target leaf spot (TLS): susceptible. Alternaria leaf spot: moderately resistant. Independent sources: a charcoal rot genotype table lists MACS 1520 with an AUDPC of 4.62 and necrosis length of 0.48, but the scale is not explained, so no rating can be confirmed. A yellow mosaic thesis tested MACS 1520 but records no resistance rating because attribution of its figures is unclear. A study of aerial blight, frogeye and anthracnose/pod blight names MACS 1520 among screened genotypes but gives no score for it. Resistance claims are therefore only partly corroborated.
pest_resistance_summary: Source of pest ratings: CSC/original variety record (not confirmed by retrieved sources). Tobacco caterpillar (S. litura): High Resistance (HR) at Indore. Stem fly and girdle beetle: Moderately Resistant (MR) at Sehore, Amravati and Parbhani. Defoliators: MR at Kota, Amravati and Parbhani. Semiloopers: MR at Indore and Parbhani. Independent sources: a 2021 Jabalpur study reports whitefly counts on MACS 1520 but covers pests only and gives no resistance rating.
drought_details_research: The digest gives no evidence that MACS 1520 is drought tolerant. A Legume Research abstract lists MACS-1520 among genotypes with low root-to-shoot ratios, and the authors link higher ratios to drought tolerance, so this points away from tolerance but does not establish susceptibility. The CSC record states that the variety gave the highest yield (ranking first) over three years in coordinated Central Zone trials, which is described as indicating tolerance to abiotic stresses. That statement is generic and does not name drought specifically, and it is not confirmed by the retrieved sources. The ARI 2018-19 report describes stable, high yields in Central Zone trials.
heat_details_research: No direct evidence found for heat tolerance in the searched sources. A 2021 Jabalpur study reported whitefly counts correlated positively with maximum temperature, but that study covers pest counts and not heat tolerance of the variety.

disease_resistance_summary: Red rot: moderately resistant, per the TNAU climate-requirement table and the Appunu et al. abstract. No other disease resistance was found in the searched sources.
pest_resistance_summary: Early shoot borer and internode borer: moderately tolerant, with antibiosis linked to phenols, proteinase inhibitors and silicon. The SBI research page suggests the variety as a donor for borer tolerance. The ResearchGate source carrying a similar statement is unverified (its page title does not match the content) and is not used as primary evidence. The SBI page also states the variety can be grown in borer-endemic areas and used in IPM; this is attributed to the SBI page only.
drought_details_research: Described as highly drought tolerant and early maturing in the Appunu et al. (2017) abstract. A field-growth study ranks Co 06022 among clones with greater ability to partition dry matter into canes under drought and a higher stress tolerance index. The TNAU table lists it as tolerant to water-deficit stress. Pot-culture water-stress transcriptome work (2, 6 and 10 days plus recovery) classes it as drought tolerant relative to the susceptible Co 8021. Drought-responsive miRNA profiling at 10 days of drought compares Co 06022 (tolerant) with Co 8021 (susceptible). Transcriptome-derived SSR and SNP markers were discovered from the Co 06022 versus Co 8021 drought transcriptomes. The Co 06022 water-efficiency trial at SBI Coimbatore is unverified and is not used as evidence here.
heat_details_research: Classed with heat-tolerant genotypes in a seven-genotype heat-stress study. agronomic_performance_stability: CSH 24 MF is a remarkable and landmark multi-cut forage hybrid that occupies approximately one-third of the forage area in India, indicating its wide adoption and stability. It also serves as a hybrid check in national level trials for fodder yield.

drought_details_research: Terminal (post-flowering) drought is the main yield constraint for HHB 226. The hybrid is described as susceptible, with severe yield losses under terminal drought. Drought tolerance has been pursued by introgressing QTLs into an improved version of the hybrid. Trials on that improved version reported higher grain yield under non-irrigated conditions than the original parents. The best improved line (no. 63) showed 97.20% recurrent-parent genome recovery, 53.25 g grain yield per plant, 73.27% relative water content and 65.06% electrolyte leakage (reported as stress-related traits). These improved-line results are not direct evidence of tolerance in commercial HHB 226.

disease_resistance_summary: Tomato leaf curl virus (ToLCV): PVB-4 is listed in PAU's Package of Practices as a determinate variety resistant to leaf curl virus. Late blight: PVB-4 was used as a parent in a study screening hybrids for combined late blight and leaf curl resistance, but the abstract does not show PVB-4 itself as late-blight resistant, so late-blight resistance is not established for PVB-4. The Tribune 2003 late-blight note concerns a different tomato release and was discarded.
heat_details_research: No confirmed heat tolerance for PVB-4. A PAU Botany study (Ludhiana, sown January 2021) tested plant growth regulators (4-CPA and GA3) on heat-stressed PVB-4 and reported a 50.8% yield increase over its control. This result reflects a response to growth-regulator treatment under heat stress and does not establish inherent heat tolerance of the untreated variety. A PAU College of Horticulture page states that a variety is tolerant to high temperature, but the text sits between two entries, so it cannot be confirmed as applying to PVB-4.

disease_resistance_summary: Yellow rust: The ICAR-IIWBR compendium describes HPW 368 as resistant to yellow and brown rust. The variety record states that over two years of All India coordinated trials/nurseries it showed resistance to yellow rust under natural field and artificial conditions compared with checks HS 240, HS 507 and VL 804, and a high degree of field resistance under artificial conditions. Brown (leaf) and stripe rust: the variety record reports seedling resistance to leaf and stripe rusts (AICW and BIP Progress Report, Vol. III, 2014, cited in the record without a URL). Powdery mildew: the variety record reports moderate resistance under natural field and artificial conditions relative to the checks. Postulated seedling resistance genes differ from the checks (Lr23+ and Yr2+ per the record). A 2023 Northern Hill Zone study used HPW 368 only as a check and reports no resistance scores for it, so it is not counted as independent evidence.

drought_details_research: A 2024 morpho-physiological study on irrigated and rainfed wheat (Rana et al., CSK HPKV) lists HPW 368 among seven genotypes selected for low drought susceptibility index and high drought recovery index under moisture stress. Under late sowing, the record reports a 9.13% grain yield reduction for HPW 368 versus 11.91% for check HPW 349. Under reduced fertilizer (75% of recommended), it reports the lowest yield decline (9.48%).

agronomic_performance_field_trials: (1) Trial design: tested at ICAR-VPKAS Hawalbagh, Almora (1250 m amsl) in 2002-03 under timely-sown rainfed and irrigated conditions, alpha-lattice design, 2 replications. (2) Plains, irrigated inorganic: 4.47 t/ha, 6.93% above the best check PBW 343. (3) Hills, irrigated organic: 3.34 t/ha, 7.46% above the best check VL Gehun 907. (4) Grain quality: about 10.4% average protein and 82.8 kg/hl test weight, described as suitable for chapatti making.
